must_read.title: Does Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Increase Reconstructive Risk? A Comparative Analysis of Surgical Efficiency and Microvascular Success in Advanced OSCC
must_read.title_zh: 新辅助化疗对晚期 OSCC 显微重建风险的影响
must_read.one_line: 回顾性比较新辅助化疗组与直接手术组游离皮瓣重建结果，NACT组缺血时间更短、并发症相当但伤口并发症更多。
must_read.so_what: q5相关手术决策证据，提示NACT不增加显微重建主要并发症但影响伤口愈合，可转化为临床决策参考。
must_read.caution: NACT组疾病分期更晚期（100% IV期vs39%），组间可比性存疑。
must_read.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) by evaluating its impact on surgical efficiency and postoperative morbidity in patients undergoing complex free-flap reconstruction for advanced oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). METHODS: A retrospective comparative study was conducted on 86 patients (NACT cohort: n = 20; Primary Surgery cohort: n = 66) undergoing microvascular free tissue transfer. Primary outcomes included surgical efficiency (ischemic time, total operative duration) and postoperative complications (major microvascular events vs. minor wound issues) that were evaluated. RESULTS: The NACT group presented with significantly more advanced disease (100% Stage IV vs. 39.4%; p < 0.001). Despite this higher tumor burden, the NACT cohort demonstrated significantly shorter mean ischemic times (39.0 ± 7.5 vs. 52.5 ± 17.9 min; p = 0.001) and reduced operative durations (7.5 ± 0.8 vs. 8.6 ± 1.3 h; p = 0.001). Total complication rates were comparable (35% vs. 33.3%). However, minor wound-related complications were significantly more frequent in the NACT group (30% vs. 4.5%; p = 0.004). The flap salvage rate following re-exploration was high and comparable between groups (80.0% vs. 85.7%). CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences were detected in major flap failure or vascular re-exploration, though the study was underpowered to establish definitive safety equivalence for these endpoints. In exploratory subgroup analysis of RFFF reconstructions, NACT was associated with reduced ischemic time (p = 0.017). These findings suggest that while NACT compromises soft-tissue wound healing, it does not preclude successful microvascular reconstruction when managed with appropriate perioperative care.

must_reads.title: A Global Perspective on Calibration and Standardization in Oral Cancer Screening Training
must_reads.title_zh: 口腔癌筛查培训的校准与标准化全球视角
must_reads.one_line: 叙述性综述梳理全球口腔癌筛查 Examiner 培训与校准现状，指出AI和移动健康是未来方向。
must_reads.so_what: 与q5（口腔鳞癌）部分相关，但聚焦诊断培训而非免疫微环境或微生物组机制。可借鉴AI辅助筛查思路。
must_reads.caution: 叙述性综述非系统评价，无量化证据合成；AI部分仅为展望。
must_reads.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early oral cancer detection improves survival, but diagnosing early, asymptomatic lesions remains challenging. Screening effectiveness depends heavily on examiner competency, highlighting the need for structured training and calibration. OBJECTIVE: This narrative review examines the evolution, current practices, and future directions of examiner training, calibration, and standardization in global oral cancer screening. REVIEW FINDINGS: Existing training programs vary widely in content, duration, and assessment. While structured approaches combining theoretical instruction, image-based learning, and supervised clinical training enhance diagnostic accuracy, published studies provide limited details on training protocols, calibration procedures, and competency benchmarks. Formal assessment of inter-examiner reliability, periodic recalibration, and standardized quality assurance are inconsistently reported. Models like OralDETECT demonstrate scalable, competency-based frameworks. Additionally, empowering community health workers through artificial intelligence, mobile health, and adjunctive diagnostic tools provides promising opportunities to expand screening capacity in resource-limited settings. CONCLUSION: Establishing an internationally standardized framework for examiner training, competency assessment, and continuous quality assurance is essential to improve screening reliability and reduce global oral cancer mortality. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Structured training and calibration bridge critical diagnostic gaps among primary healthcare practitioners. Integrating these standardized protocols with digital health innovations enhances triage accuracy, overcomes geographic barriers, and optimizes risk-based screening models.

scan.title: Three-dimensional reconstruction of ultrasound imaging in dentistry: a systematic review
scan.title_zh: 牙科超声成像三维重建系统评价
scan.one_line: 系统评价13项研究，机械扫描与机器人控制精度更高。
scan.so_what: 与q4（材料表面评估）间接相关，成像方法可迁移至材料表征。
scan.caution: 多数为体外研究，临床适用性有限。
scan.abstract: BACKGROUND: Three-dimensional ultrasound (3D-US) reconstruction has emerged as a potential solution to the limited field of view and operator dependence of two-dimensional intraoral ultrasonography. Multiple acquisition, tracking, and reconstruction strategies have been proposed, yet no prior systematic review has synthesized the methods used specifically within dentistry. OBJECTIVE: To identify and compare 3D-US reconstruction techniques applied in dentistry and evaluate how acquisition strategy, spatial tracking, and reconstruction methodology influence accuracy, reproducibility, feasibility, and clinical applicability. METHODS: A systematic search of 5 databases was performed. Studies were included in the review if they used ultrasound imaging with any 3D-US reconstruction method for a defined dental application. Risk of bias was assessed using a customized hybrid QUADAS-2/QUIN/STARD framework. RESULTS: Thirteen studies (2010-2025) met the inclusion criteria; 10 were in vitro and 3 in vivo. Acquisition methods included mechanized linear-stage scanning (n = 6), robotic arm control (n = 2), tracked freehand (n = 2), untracked freehand (n = 1), and custom intraoral jigs (n = 2). Accuracy ranged from 12 to 50 μm for digital impressions to sub-millimeter deviations for periodontal and ridge assessments, with most error rates below 10%. Reproducibility and clinical feasibility were both inversely related to hardware complexity: mechanized and robotic systems achieved the highest precision and enabled precise positioning for repeated evaluations; however, they had the lowest clinical usability. Conversely, freehand approaches demonstrated the strongest clinical potential but at the expense of reproducible positioning and highly precise measurements. Risk of bias was high or unclear in all studies due to heterogeneity, small sample sizes, and limited in vivo validation. CONCLUSIONS: Over 15 years, 3D-US reconstruction in dentistry has advanced substantially, demonstrating promising accuracy for digital impressions, periodontal assessment, ridge measurement, and implant planning. However, most studies remain feasibility-based and in vitro, and methodological variation limits comparability.
